2026-09-29 — caution (from Claude)
After Jason's first message asking for info, the seller edited the ad to add a phone number that belongs to someone else (maybe a partner). Weak alone; notable with the $8k ask (~55% under fair), a year listed, and the $12.5k -> $8k cut. Unproven, not a scam call.
VERIFY before anything else:
1. Answers in Messenger first (VIN, title photo, why the price cut). If calling the number, ask who they are and their tie to the car.
2. Oregon title photo showing the VIN; name must match the FB seller or the person on the phone. Won't show it = walk.
3. Run the VIN: Carfax + an NMVTIS title report (brands from every state). Must decode to a 1999 M Roadster.
4. Live video walkaround: VIN plate, odometer, the torn driver seat, cold start.
5. Search the phone number (Google, FB Marketplace) for reuse across car ads.
6. Jason picks the Medford PPI shop; seller drops the car off.
STOP IF: deposit to hold it, payment before seeing it, shipping/agent/escrow he picks, gift cards/Zelle, can't meet, VIN/title mismatch. No personal details beyond name until the title checks out.

The listing states 2 owners. The Carfax shows 3 owners (1999, 2003, 2005).

critical_evidence.evidence: Jason asked about the trunk subframe welds. The owner answered only where they are, not their condition, and sent no photos. There is no reinforcement record. The 2016 Carfax rear/right-rear damage and the 2012 total-loss collision make this inspection more important.
The Carfax has no reported cooling-system entry. No receipts were provided. The car saw about 600 miles from 2016 to 2025, so the rubber and plastics have aged even at low mileage.
This is a 1999 car with the S52 engine (confirmed by VIN decode). The S54 rod-bearing issue applies only to 2001–2002 S54 cars.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: a decoded VIN and a full Carfax with title and odometer history. The maintenance and repair half is missing. There are no total-loss repair invoices (claimed but not sent), no cooling, VANOS or subframe records, no trunk-floor photos, and the title is not in hand.

condition.rationale: Observed problems: torn driver seat cushion, worn and soiled door cards, and a rear vinyl window being replaced. The car has an insurance total-loss collision with no repair evidence and later rear damage. It sat at about 600 miles in 9 years with no reported age-related service. Paint looks good in the photos, but nothing structural or mechanical is proven.

price_value.rationale: The $8,000 ask is far below the $16,704–$21,317 fair-value band. However, an insurance total-loss history materially discounts both value and resale. Title and estate paperwork are unresolved, and catch-up from storage plus interior work is likely. The discount is large but largely explained by the known history.

mission_fit.rationale: The car is a manual and its price is below the ideal band, which fits the bridge brief. Against that, the total-loss Carfax hurts 6–24-month resale. Reliability after long storage is unproven. Title timing may delay availability, and a Z3 M is profiled as a keeper rather than a bridge.

logistics.rationale: Talent, OR is about 400 miles from Carmel, and an in-person viewing is offered. A PPI with a BMW or collision specialist in the Medford area should be arrangeable. The title is not in hand, estate authority is unproven, and an Oregon-to-California transfer requires smog and VIN verification.

ppi_focus: Collision-repair assessment for the 2012 total loss: panel gaps, paint meter readings, frame/unibody measurements, welds, seam sealer, airbag and SRS system status.
Rear subframe mounts, trunk-floor spot welds and differential mount ears inspected from the trunk and from below (any cracking or tearing), especially given the 2016 right-rear damage.
Cooling system: water pump, thermostat, radiator and expansion-tank plastics, hoses, fan clutch; pressure test.
VANOS rattle and function, valve-cover and oil-filter-housing leaks, and a scan for stored codes and OBD readiness for CA smog.
Storage effects: fuel system, brake fluid and caliper function, belts, tire date codes and flat-spotting.
Rear trailing-arm bushings, shock mounts, and motor/transmission mounts.
Clutch engagement and slip, shift quality, differential noise.
Soft-top mechanism and frame, plus confirmation of the new rear window installation and seal.
Rust at rockers, floors and jacking points.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: total-loss repair invoices and photos showing a professional repair, plus a clean specialist PPI including structural measurements and rear subframe and trunk welds.
Up: a duplicate title in hand with no brand, together with valid estate authority paperwork.
Up: cooling receipts, or a price that absorbs a full cooling refresh and seat repair.
Down: any cracking at the trunk floor or diff mounts, frame misalignment, or evidence of a poor collision repair.
Down: a branded title appears, or the estate paperwork cannot be produced.
evidence.mission_note: It is a manual S52 M Roadster priced below the ideal band, which matches the enthusiast-bridge brief on spec and price. The insurance total-loss history and unresolved estate title weaken quick, low-risk resale and immediate availability. A Z3 M is also profiled as a keeper rather than a bridge.
evidence.rationale: The VIN and Carfax establish a genuine 1999 S52 manual M Roadster with a consistent odometer trail (66,288 mi in 10/2025) and one Oregon owner from 2005 to the present. The same Carfax shows an insurance total-loss declaration with collision damage in 11/2012 and separate rear/right-rear damage in 2016. The owner's text reduces this to 'an accident' that was repaired, with receipts claimed but not supplied. The photos show glossy paint and stock wheels and exhaust, but also two tears in the driver seat cushion and worn door cards, and the owner says the rear vinyl window is being replaced. The title is not in hand (a duplicate is on order) and the registered owner is deceased, so title brand status and the seller's authority remain open. The model-critical rear-structure evidence is missing: the weld-condition question went unanswered, which matters more given the rear damage history. There is no reported cooling-system entry in 27 years, and very low use since 2016 implies storage-related aging. The $8,000 ask sits far below the $16,704–$21,317 fair-value band, a gap largely accounted for by the total-loss history and paperwork uncertainty.
evidence.next_action: Ask the seller: Can you send photos or scans of the 2012 accident repair receipts, showing what panels and parts were replaced and by which shop?
